### page_2
Eastern Variscan fold belt: Paleomagnetic evidence
for oroclinal bending
J. A. Tait Institute fu ¨r Allgemeine und Angewandte Geophysik, Ludwig-Maximilians Universita ¨t, Theresienstrasse 41,
80333 Mu ¨nchen, GermanyV. Bachtadse
H. Soffel
ABSTRACT
The Rhenohercynian zone of Variscan Europe trends from
southernPortugal,aroundtheIbero-Armoricanarc,intosouthern
Britain,Belgium,northernGermany,andtheMoravo-Silesianzone
oftheeastCzechRepublic.Althoughthegeodynamicevolutionof
thecentralandwesternsegmentsofthisarcuatebeltisnowfairly
wellunderstood,thescenarioforthemoreeasterlypartsremains
enigmatic.ApaleomagneticstudyofUpperDevonianrocksfrom
theMoravo-Silesianzonehasbeenundertaken.Twoancientdirec-
tionsofmagnetizationhavebeenidentiﬁed.Theﬁrst(theAmag-
netization)issecondaryinoriginandrelatestoaremagnetization
ofPermian-Carboniferousage.TheBmagnetizationpassesthefold
test, is considered Late Devonian in age, and agrees in terms of
inclinationtopreviouslypublishedpaleomagneticresultsfromco-
evalrocksoftheHarzMountainsandFranconianForest,central
Europe.Thedeclination,however,differsbyabout90 &.Restoring
the Moravo-Silesian zone to its original Devonian orientation as
deﬁnedbythenewpaleomagneticdatabringsthestructuraltrends
ofcentralandeasternEuropeintoagreement.Becausetheywere
previouslypartofthesametectonostratigraphicunit,assuggested
bythestratigraphicrecord,thisimpliesthatrotationaloroclinal
bendingaroundthenorthernandeasternﬂanksoftheBohemian
massif occurred sometime between the Late Devonian and Late
Carboniferous.
INTRODUCTION
Several models have been proposed to explain the arcuate
shapeoftheVariscanfoldbeltinEurope.WithregardtotheIbero-
Armoricanarc,Carey(1955)originallypostulatedsecondarypro-
cesseswithbendingofanoriginallystraightbelt.Ithassincebeen
demonstrated,however,thatthisarcwastosomeextentprimaryin
nature,butunderwentsecondarytighteningduringtheﬁnalstages
oftheVariscanorogeny(JulivertandArboleya,1986;Pe ´rez-Estau´n
etal.,1988).Thisissupportedbythepaleomagneticrecord,which
showsaclosecorrelationbetweenthedeclinationdeviationsandthe
structuraltrend.Itisnot,however,a1:1correlationaswouldbe
expectedforpurelysecondary(oroclinal)bending(Bonhommetet
al.,1981;Eldredgeetal.,1985;Hirtetal.,1992;LowrieandHirt,
1986;Perroud,1986;Riesetal.,1980;RiesandShackleton,1976;
BachtadseandVanderVoo,1986).Variousmechanismsforthe
cause of bending throughout the fold belt have been suggested,
ranging from strike-slip models (Badham, 1982), and large-scale
shearzonesandobliquecollision(Bachtadseetal.,1983),todraping
ofthemoremobileregionsaroundrelativelystableblocks(Ziegler,
1990),ortheaccretionofmicroplatesontoirregularlyshapedcon-
tinentalmargins(Lorenz,1976).MatteandRibiero(1975),Burget
al.(1981),andMatteandBurg(1981)suggestedthatthearcuate
shapeoftheIbero-Armoricanarcwascausedbyindentationofa
southern continental promontory, or microplate (Ziegler, 1990;
Riding,1974),intothenortherncontinents.Thismodelissupported
bypaleomagneticevidence(Hirtetal.,1992;Pare ´setal.,1994).
Thesituationforthemoreeasternpartsofthebeltisnotso
clear.CorrelationoftheRhenohercynianwiththeMoravo-Silesian
zonesoutheastoftheBohemianmassifhasbeenmadeonthebasis
ofstructuralandstratigraphicevidence.Ithasbeenproposedthat
theywereformerlyconnectedbyanarcuatestructurearoundthe
easternﬂankoftheBohemianmassif,whichhassubsequentlybeen
obliteratedbyfaultingalongthesouthwestmarginoftheEastern
European platform (Burchette, 1981; Franke, 1989). However,
whetherthearcwasprimaryinorigin,orsecondaryandresulting
fromoroclinalbendingoftheRhenohercynianaroundtheBohe-
mianmassif,isnotknown.
Inordertoestablishthestructuralrelationshipbetweenthese
tworegions,andtotestfororoclinalbendingintheeasternsector
oftheVariscanfoldbelt,apaleomagneticstudyofDevoniansed-
imentaryandvolcanicrocksfromMoraviahasbeencarriedout.
GEOLOGY
The Moravo-Silesian zone is separated to the west from the
Moldanubianzonebyanorthwest-dipping,dextraltranspressional
zoneofstrikeslip(Schulmannetal.,1991).Thisshearzonewas
activeinlatePaleozoictimeandprobablyreﬂectsreactivationofan
older southeast-facing thrust (Matte, 1991). Basement rocks of
Moravo-Silesian are composed of Cadomian granitoids (e.g., the
Brnopluton)thathavelatePrecambrian–EarlyCambrian(550–580
Ma)intrusionages(ScharbertandBatik,1980;SoraufandJa ¨ger,
1982;vanBreemenetal.,1982).Theseareoverlainwithanero-
sional unconformity by thin epicontinental Middle Devonian red
sandstones, conglomerates, spilitic submarine volcanic rocks, and
Upper Devonian–Lower Carboniferous reef carbonates of the
MoravianKarst(Fig.1).
Deformationintheregionincreasestowardthenorthwestern
marginwiththeMoldanubian,andalsoalongstriketothenortheast,
suchthattothesouthwestthebasementandcoverrocksareonly
weakly deformed, whereas to the northeast they are strongly
shearedwithnortheast-southwestlineationandnorthwest-dipping
foliation.Thisdeformationisrelatedtopost-Devoniannortheast-
directed thrusting of the Moldanubian over Moravia (Fritz and
Neubauer,1995;Matteetal.,1990).Ithasbeensuggestedthatthis
obliquecollisionanddextraltranspressiveregime,whichisalsore-
corded in the structural record of Devonian sequences along the
northwestMoravianmargin(Rajlich,1989),aretheresultofinden-
tation of the Moldanubian with Moravo-Silesia (Fritz and
Neubauer, 1991). The Carboniferous foredeep has also been
stronglydeformedwithuprightnortheast-southwest–trendingfolds
with steeply dipping cleavage and horizontal lineation fabrics re-
lated to transpressional dextral tectonics. Dextral transpressional
movementalongtheMoldanubianboundaryisdeterminedstrati-
graphically as post-Namurian and pre-Permian, and by
40Ar/39Ar
plateauagesof305–310Mafromassociatedgneisses(Matteetal.,
1990;seealsoDallmeyeretal.,1995).

Becauseoflimitedoutcropconditionsandtherelativelyhigh
degreeofdeformationandmetamorphismprevalentintheMoravo-
Silesianzone,samplingwasrestrictedtosevenseparatelocalities
(Fig.1).ThesamplescompriseMiddleDevonianclasticsediments
(BRNandZNO);Givetian-FrasnianJosefovreeflimestones(JED)

PALEOMAGNETICRESULTS
All samples were thermally demagnetized, and results were
analyzedusingorthogonalvectorplots(Zijderveld,1967)andste-
reographicprojection.Thedirectionsofthelinearsegmentswere
calculated using the principal component analysis of Kirschvink
(1980),andstatisticswerecalculatedinallcasesaccordingtoFisher
(1953).Themagneticmineralogywasdeterminedusingisothermal
remanentmagnetization(IRM)techniques,andthermaldemagne-
tizationofthesaturationIRM(SIRM).Althoughnoneofthesam-
pleshasundergoneanyapparentpenetrativedeformation,thean-
isotropyofmagneticsusceptibilitywasmeasuredonanumberof
samplesfromeachrocktypeusingaKLY-2Kappabridge.There-
sultsshowthat,forallrocktypes,onlyverylowdegreesofmagnetic
grainalignment(generally1%–2%)arepresent,indicatingthatno
secondaryfabricshavebeenimpressedontherocks.
Reliablemagnetizationdirectionscouldonlybeidentiﬁedfrom
thesedimentarysamples.Duringthermaldemagnetization,thevol-
canicrocksweremagneticallyunstableandfailedtorevealanycon-
sistent magnetization direction at site level. These samples were
collectedfromthenortheasternpartoftheMoravianzonewhere
deformationandmetasomaticactivityaremorepronounced,and
theseresultsarenotdiscussed.
Thesandstoneandcarbonatesamplesshowdistinctbehavior
during thermal treatment. After removal of a low-temperature
(,200 8C)componentthatisgenerallysimilartothelocalpresent-
dayﬁelddirection,uptotwodirectionsofmagnetization,AandB,
canbeisolated.TheMiddleDevoniansandstonesshowfairlystable
behaviorwithremovalofashallowsoutherlyAdirectionofmag-
netization between 200 and 5808C, during which the intensity of
magnetizationremainsrelativelyconstant,andthedemagnetization
trajectoryoftenfollowsagreatcirclepath(Fig.2A).Above580 8C,
ahigh-temperaturecomponent(magnetizationB)canbeidentiﬁed
thatisofmixedpolarityafterbeddingcorrection.IRMexperiments
andsubsequentthermaldemagnetizationofthesaturationmagne-
tization conﬁrm the predominance of hematite as the magnetic
carrier.
Thecarbonatesamplescanbesubdividedintotwosubgroups
accordingtotheirdemagnetizationbehaviorandlithology.Theﬁne-
grainedgrayHadylimestonesbelongtotheﬁrstcategory,inwhich
both the A and B magnetizations can be clearly identiﬁed after
removalofapresent-dayoverprint(Fig.2B).MagnetizationAis
southerly and shallow and is removed between 200 and 3508C,
whereasmagnetizationBrepresentsthestableend-pointdirection.
It has unblocking temperatures of 500–5308C and is directed
towardtheeastwithintermediatenegativeandpositiveinsituin-
clinationvalues.Theinterpretationthatthiscomponentiscarried
bymagnetiteissupportedbyIRMandthermaldemagnetizationof
SIRMexperiments.Theseshowthepresenceofonlyonemagnetic
carrierthatsaturatesinlowﬁelds( ,100mT)andhasunblocking
temperaturesof500–5808C.
Thegray,pinkish-gray,andredKrtinyandJosefovlimestones
showdifferentbehavior.TheygenerallyhavestrongerNRMinten-
sitiesthantheHadyBergcarbonates,buttheAmagnetizationdom-
inatesthesignal.InmostKrtinysamples,theAmagnetizationrep-
resents the stable end point, but in some of the red samples the
demagnetizationtrajectoriesarenotdirectedtowardtheoriginbut
areslightlycurved,indicatingthepresenceofasecond,highertem-
perature(.550 8C)componentofmagnetization.However,thein-
tensityofmagnetizationatthesetemperaturesisverylow,andthe
greatcirclesarenotdeﬁnedwellenoughforinterpretation.Forthe
redandpinkishJosefovlimestones,theAmagnetizationisdomi-
nant,anddemagnetizationtrajectoriesfollowagreatcirclepathat
highertemperatures.StableendpointsfortheBcomponentcanbe

INTERPRETATION
Inadditiontoapresent-dayoverprint,twoancientdirectionsof
magnetizationcanbeidentiﬁedintheseMiddletoUpperDevonian
rocks.TheAmagnetizationisofsinglepolarity,andyieldsanoverall
meandirectionof202 8/038,k 512.8, a
95 519.58(sixsites)insitu,
and 1958/108,k 56.5, a95 528.38after bedding correction (Ta-
ble1).Itfailsthefoldtest,demonstratingthatacquisitionpostdates
deformationandisthereforeofsecondaryorigin.
Deformation continued in the eastern Moravo-Silesian zone
untilUpperCarboniferoustime,asdemonstratedbythehighlyde-
formed sediments of the Carboniferous foredeep, and the ﬁnal
transpressional movements along the Moldanubian-Moravian
boundary to the west occurred sometime between the Namurian
andStephanian.Thisimplies,therefore,aLateCarboniferousage
ofdeformation.Comparingthepaleopolepositionof42 8S,3548E
derivedfromAwiththeCarboniferous-PermiansectoroftheEu-
ropeanapparentpolarwanderpath(VanderVoo,1993),itclearly
coincideswiththeUpperCarboniferoussegmentandisthusinter-
pretedasreﬂectinganoverprinteventofthisage.
TheBmagnetizationisgenerallyisolatedasstraight-lineseg-
mentsdirectedtowardtheorigininorthogonalprojection.Identi-
ﬁedinsixsites,itisofmixedpolarity,andyieldsanoverallmean
directionof091 8/2088,k 58.8, a
95 523.98insitu,and089 8/2378,
k 517.9, a95 516.38afterbeddingcorrection(Table1B,Fig.3).
The improvement in clustering of the site mean directions after
beddingcorrectionissigniﬁcantatthe95%levelofconﬁdenceusing
thefoldtestofMcFadden(1990).Becausefoldingwasinitiatedin
lowermostCarboniferoustimeinthisregion,acloserelationship
between the magnetization and rock ages is implied, and the B
magnetizationisthusconsideredprimaryinorigin.
However,itshouldbepointedoutthatthesitemeandirections
havelarge a
95 values,asdoestheoverallmeandirection,andthe
reversaltestofMcFaddenandMcElhinny(1990)isinconclusive.
Thisisrelatedtothestrongoverprintdirectionsmakingisolationof

Devonian),andminorrelativerotationsmayhaveoccurredbetween

DISCUSSIONANDCONCLUSIONS
InvertingtheoverallmeandirectionforcomponentBintoits
reversedpolarity(2698/1378)allowsdirectcomparisonwithprevi-
ouslypublishedpaleomagneticdatafromotherVariscanmassifsin
centralEurope(Fig.4).Withintheerrorlimits,theinclinationvalue
forBisinreasonableagreementwiththedataofBachtadseetal.
(1983).However,comparingthedeclinationvalues,itisclearthat
theMoravo-Silesianzonehasrotated ;908clockwisesincetheLate
Devonian,withrespecttotheGermansegmentsofthebelt.Anti-
clockwiserotationoftheMoravo-Silesianzoneby90 8bringsboth
thepaleomagneticdeclinationandstructuraltrendintoagreement
withthoseoftheRhenohercynianzoneofcentralEurope.Because
they were formerly part of the same tectonostratigraphic unit, as
indicatedinthegeologicrecord,thisimpliesthatrotationalorocli-
nalbendinghasoccurredaroundthenortheastﬂankoftheBohe-
mianmassif.Thetimingofthisrotationcanbebracketedbycom-
ponentA,whichwasacquiredintheUpperCarboniferousandis
notrotated.Themechanismresponsibleforbendingremainsun-
clear, but a likely contender would be that of indentation of the
BohemianmassifintotheRhenohercynian.
